notes.text: Konsta Helenius is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games.
Ryan McLeod returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 7% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Patrick Kane is day to day and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Tyler Bertuzzi has taken his spot beside Connor Bedard and Roman Kantserov. That line has had 38% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 40:41 together, about what it had with Kane (41%).

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve and has missed the last 11 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 29% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 118:24 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.

stakes: The Sabres go in sixth in the Atlantic with 19 points, the Blackhawks eighth in the Central with 9 points.

CHI.body: Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Chicago has home-ice advantage. The Blackhawks’ best way to tip it is a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: Something has to change for the Blackhawks
paras: The Blackhawks are winless in six (0-5-1), and the Sabres (8-7-3) lost 8-3 to Tampa Bay last night. The Sabres won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in Buffalo on Oct 3. Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last in the Central (31st).

The Sabres’ record (.528) is about what their chances are worth. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.250) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .361, and their goaltending has held them back.

This season, the Sabres have been outscored 64-53, but only 39-37 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 20-10. In their six-game skid, the Blackhawks have been outscored 32-13, including 23-10 at 5-on-5.

The Blackhawks (32nd) and the Sabres (30th) both don't block many shots. The Sabres get their shots through to the net (4th) and get their defensemen shooting (5th). As for the Blackhawks, they have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also pick their shots (2nd lowest), so the Blackhawks may have a hard time getting pucks to the net against the Sabres. Chicago has scored 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league, and allowed 4.22, the second most. The Sabres wait for good looks, but the Hawks settle for hopeful ones.

Tage Thompson (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 18 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Chicago. Jack Quinn (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 18 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Roman Kantserov (9 G / 2 A / 11 P in 18 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Colten Ellis (3-3-0 / .873 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to start for Buffalo, and Spencer Knight (4-10-0 / .881 SV% in 14 GS) for Chicago.
The Sabres usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
